entry.title: I stopped treating AI spend and doomscrolling as separate problems — 7 fixes that shipped real work
entry.summary:
Last month I kept asking the same question: why am I "busy" all day but shipping so little? Two things were happening at once: my AI coding costs kept jumping week to week my attention kept getting nuked by feeds between coding blocks I treated them as two separate problems for way too long. feedback loops. When you can't see cost in real time, you overspend. Here are the 7 fixes that actually worked for me. I now keep token/cost visibility in front of me during sessions. That one change killed the "one more retry" spiral. I used to default to expensive models for everything. heavy reasoning: premium model boilerplate/refactors/docs: cheaper model Most work does not need top-tier reasoning. Before hitting enter, I ask: what exact output do I need? what files are actually relevant? what's the smallest acceptable pass? This alone reduced wasteful reruns a lot. Deleting apps never lasted. I can still use DMs, search, and direct messages without infinite scroll. Open-ended AI sessions are where costs explode. I track: biggest expensive session why it blew up one rule to prevent repeat Tiny review, big compounding gains. No feeds, no notifications, one coding objective. TokenBar ($5): menu bar visibility for token/cost usage while coding → https://tokenbar.site
Monk Mode ($15): feed-level blocking on Mac so work blocks stay clean → https://mac.monk-mode.lifestyle
Both came from solving my own workflow mess as a solo builder. If your AI bill feels random and your focus feels fragmented, try treating them as one system problem for a week. You'll probably ship more and spend less.

entry.title: How do you actually get back into a project after being away for a few days?
entry.summary:
Every time I switch back to a project I haven't touched in a few days, I lose 1-2 hours just trying to remember where I left off. I work across 3 projects at once. The switching itself is fine — it's the coming back that kills me. What was I doing? Why did I stop? What did the team decide last week? I'll dig through Slack, reread notes, check the task board — and still feel like my brain hasn't fully loaded in yet. Is this just the cost of juggling multiple projects, or have you found something that actually helps? Asking because I'm trying to figure out if this is a me problem or a everyone problem. If you've got a system that works — even a messy one — I'd genuinely love to hear it. How do you actually get back into a project after being away for a few days?
